name: FLORES-200
description: FLORES-200 is a benchmark dataset for machine translation between English and low-resource languages. It consists of 3001 sentences extracted from 842 distinct web articles, covering a variety of topics and domains. These sentences have been professionally translated into 200 languages, enabling evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems. The dataset is divided into three splits: dev, devtest, and test.

rai:dataCollection: Sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia, covering three domains: Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (age-appropriate nonfiction books for children), and WikiVoyage (travel guides). The sentence selection process involved selecting an article at random from each source, then manually selecting 3-5 contiguous sentences from each article. Sentences were balanced across document locations (beginning, middle, end). The selection was performed by 10 annotators with diverse backgrounds and regions of origin.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Sentences were sourced from English Wikipedia articles across three domains: Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage. All source sentences were extracted from English Wikipedia to enable many-to-many evaluation while ensuring consistent source material.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Automatic quality control checks were implemented including: (1) language identification, (2) checking for source sentence copying, (3) checking for significant length differences, (4) checking translation fluency via language model, and (5) checking for verbatim copying from publicly available translation engines. A heuristic was developed to detect and reject translations that were likely copies from translation engines based on sentence-level similarity (spBLEU threshold of 50 with difference >20 between engines). Translations with more than 10% of sentences violating these criteria were sent for re-translation before human evaluation.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Professional translators translated sentences from English (or Spanish, French, Russian, Modern Standard Arabic for some languages) into 200 target languages through Language Service Providers (LSPs). The workflow included: (1) translation by LSP, (2) editing within LSP, (3) automated quality control checks, (4) human quality assessment by independent LSP evaluators who provided translation quality scores (0-100 scale) based on error categories (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, register). Translations scoring below 90% were sent for re-translation. Multiple rounds of re-translation and evaluation were conducted until quality threshold was met. Error severity levels were classified as critical, major, or minor.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed through a Translation Quality Score (0-100 scale) based on identified errors across nine categories: grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register. Each error was associated with a severity level (minor, major, critical). The largest error category across all languages was mistranslation. The acceptable translation quality score threshold was set at 90%. Evaluators paid particular attention to unnatural translation errors.
rai:dataBiases: The authors note that source sentences are extracted from English Wikipedia and translated into other languages, which introduces translationese effects. While the authors conjecture these effects are marginal when evaluating low-resource language models, the dataset inherently reflects English-centric content and perspectives. The selection of topics and domains (news, children's books, travel) may not represent all cultural contexts equally.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset consists of translationese (translations from English or other pivot languages) rather than naturally occurring text in target languages, which has known idiosyncrasies. The source content is limited to Wikipedia domains (news, children's books, travel guides), which may not represent all text types or domains. Some languages have very limited training data available, making translation particularly challenging. The evaluation is limited to sentence-level translation and does not capture discourse-level phenomena.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for: (1) Evaluation of machine translation systems, particularly for low-resource and multilingual translation, (2) Benchmarking many-to-many multilingual translation models, (3) Evaluation of translation quality across 200 languages and 10,100 language pairs, (4) Document-level translation evaluation (sentences from same article are contiguous), (5) Multimodal translation evaluation (metadata includes image and hyperlink information). The dataset supports the WMT Large-Scale Multilingual Machine Translation shared task.
rai:annotationsPerItem: Each translation received human quality assessment by independent evaluators. For languages requiring re-translation, multiple rounds of evaluation were conducted. On average, 45 languages required re-translation with an average of 1 re-translation per language (maximum 3 re-translations).
rai:annotatorDemographics: The sentence selection process was performed by 10 annotators: 6 male and 4 female, with different roles (researchers, scientists, engineers, program/project managers), originally from different regions (East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, North America). Professional translators were used for translation, though specific demographic information about translators is not provided.
